subtopics.title: Why the State Steps In — and With What

questions.question: Which of these is a reason for public sector intervention in markets?
options: Externalities like factory smoke appear on nobody's invoice, so the market overlooks them

questions.question: VAT, excise duties, the fuel levy and the sugary drinks levy are examples of:
options: Indirect taxes — levied on goods and services, raising revenue and steering behaviour

questions.question: A subsidy is best described as:
options: Taxation in reverse — the state pays part of a good's cost so it reaches consumers cheaper
A loan that must be repaid monthly

questions.question: Social grants, public clinics and no-fee schools belong to the WELFARE family because they:
options: Bypass prices entirely — placing buying power or services directly with households

subtopics.title: Taxes and Subsidies on the Diagram

questions.question: An indirect tax on a good shifts:
options: The supply curve LEFTWARD — sellers need a higher price at every quantity
Neither curve; only the label changes

questions.question: After the tax, the equilibrium price typically rises by LESS than the full tax because:
options: The state refunds part of the tax
The burden is shared — sellers absorb part and buyers pay the rest
Buyers refuse to pay any increase

questions.question: A subsidy on commuter transport results in:
options: Supply shifting rightward — lower fares and more passengers riding

questions.question: An honest account of taxes and subsidies includes which possible misfires?
options: Taxes always end smuggling; subsidies always reach consumers
Both instruments are free to administer
A too-high tax breeds illicit trade, and a careless subsidy can be pocketed by producers instead of cutting prices

questions.question: A maximum price is set:
options: BELOW equilibrium, to keep an essential affordable for buyers

questions.question: The shortage under a binding ceiling is PERMANENT because:
options: The one force that could clear it — a rising price — is against the law
The state keeps buying the stock

questions.question: With price rationing switched off, the good is allocated by:
options: A national lottery run by the treasury
Queues, favoured customers, per-family limits — and luck or connections

questions.question: The black market under a ceiling is born from:
options: The gap between what the law permits and what the shelves hold — the desperate pay above the ceiling illegally

subtopics.title: Minimum Prices and the Minimum Wage — the Floor

questions.question: A minimum price set above equilibrium produces:
options: A SURPLUS — quantity supplied exceeds quantity demanded and stock piles up

questions.question: Because the price may not fall to clear the surplus, the state typically must:
options: Buy the surplus, store it, export it, or watch it spoil — with the bill landing in the budget

questions.question: The minimum wage is a price floor in which market?
options: The LABOUR market — households sell labour and firms buy it

questions.question: The mature conclusion on the minimum wage is that:
options: The diagram proves it can never help workers
The diagram proves it can never cost jobs
It trades protecting the employed against risking the excluded — and the size of that trade-off is measured empirically, not settled by the diagram

questions.question: The referee's four calls are:
options: Make it dearer (tax), make it cheaper (subsidy), freeze the score (price controls), hand the ball over (welfare)

questions.question: The sugary drinks levy performs two jobs with one call:
options: Raising revenue AND nudging buyers toward less harmful choices
Freezing the price and rationing by queue

questions.question: The state steps onto the pitch at all because:
options: Society sometimes refuses to apply "whoever can pay, plays" to bread, medicine or wages
The rules require a minimum number of officials

subtopics.title: Ceilings Make Queues, Floors Make Piles

questions.question: Under the cooking oil ceiling, the shelves go bare because:
options: Shoppers pour in at the low price while producers, barely paid, produce less — and the price may not rise to call more in
The state bought all the oil

questions.question: The bottles sold quietly at double behind the shop represent:
options: The black market — trading in the space between what the law permits and what the shelves hold

questions.question: Under the guaranteed potato price, the warehouse fills because:
options: Growers plant less at high prices
Buyers purchase more at high prices
Growers plant every field while buyers take fewer bags — and the price may not drop to clear the stock

questions.question: The memory trick pairs:
options: Queues with floors and piles with ceilings
Queues with subsidies and piles with taxes
Queues with equilibrium and piles with shortage
QUEUES under low-pressed ceilings; PILES stacked on jacked-up floors

subtopics.title: The Wage Floor at the Factory Gate

questions.question: Without any wage rule, the wage for unskilled work at the packhouse gate settles:
options: Where the crowd of work-seekers meets the firm's hiring plans — possibly below what rent and food cost
At the highest wage in the industry

questions.question: Truth one about the wage floor is that:
options: Employed workers' lives genuinely improve, and their spending feeds the neighbourhood's circular flow
It applies only to skilled work

questions.question: Truth two warns that the workers squeezed out first are:
options: The youngest and least experienced — the very group the floor was built to protect

questions.question: The three-question habit for judging ANY intervention is:
options: Who proposed it, who opposed it, who voted?
How much, how soon, how loud?
Is it old, is it new, is it foreign?
What was it FOR, what does the diagram predict, and what ELSE follows?
